<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead" summary="Build app shell and navigation">
Full UI/navigation pass on /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm — the app works but has NO navigation: the header is still stock Phoenix (Website/GitHub/Get Started linking to phoenixframework.org) and / is the stock Phoenix welcome page. Every surface is URL-only. Build a proper app shell. You own: lib/cleaner_crm_web/components/layouts.ex, lib/cleaner_crm_web/controllers/page_html/home.html.heex (+ page_controller/page_html if needed), small additive edits to LiveViews ONLY where a layout assign is needed, router.ex additive-only, and any new nav components. Do NOT touch business logic, contexts, or the running server/dev _build.

MCP note: on "No session_id available" add session_id "b82dc084-1093-4624-b490-31c68a31a4a8"; if MCP hangs, message me and keep coding.

FULL ROUTE INVENTORY (all exist, group them sensibly):
Office (owner/admin only, RequireOfficeRole): /schedule (board; sub: plans/new, jobs/new, cleaners/new), /clients, /quotes (+ /quotes/rate-card, /quotes/new), /invoices, /timesheets (+ csv export), /quality (review; + /quality/scorecards, /quality/templates), /reviews (inbox), /reminders (delivery log), /audit, /settings/booking (cancellation policy).
Authenticated (any user): /field (cleaner day view; owners/admins may view), /field/jobs/:id, /users/settings, /accounts (+ picker/manage/members/invitations), /integrations.
Public: / (landing), /book (instant quote), /book/accept/:token, /users/log-in, /users/register.
Portal (magic-link session): /portal, /portal/visits/:id, /portal/invoices.
Token pages (no nav needed beyond minimal branding): /reviews/:token, /pay/:token, /reminders/confirm|reschedule/:token.

REQUIREMENTS:
1. Role-aware app header/nav in layouts.app: for owner/admin — grouped nav (direct links: Schedule, Clients, Quotes, Invoices, Timesheets, Quality, Reviews; a "More" or grouped dropdown for Reminders, Audit; a Settings dropdown: Rate card, Booking policy, Accounts, Integrations, User settings) + a clearly visible "Field view" link (owners can see /field) + user dropdown (email, Settings, Log out). For plain members (cleaners) — minimal: My Day (/field), user dropdown (Settings, Log out); NO office links. Determine role via CleanerCrm.Accounts.get_user_role(scope, user.id, active_account_id) — assign once (e.g. in the existing UserAuth on_mount or a small layout helper handling nil account) rather than N calls per render; handle nil active_account_id gracefully. Current page indication (active link styling) is a plus if cheap.
2. Landing page /: replace the stock Phoenix welcome with a simple Cleaner CRM landing: product name/one-liner, primary CTA "Get an instant quote" → /book, secondary "Client portal" → /portal and "Business log in" → /users/log-in (+ Register). If current_scope is present, offer "Go to app" (office → /schedule, cleaner → /field).
3. Portal pages get a minimal portal nav (Home /portal, Invoices /portal/invoices, business name) — check how PortalLive renders today and add consistently (portal layout or shared component). Public /book + token pages: minimal branding header (logo/name + "Client portal" link), no app nav, no phoenixframework links anywhere.
4. Keep DaisyUI + the theme_toggle; mobile responsive (nav collapses into the existing hamburger pattern at small widths — that pattern already exists, extend it). No data-confirm; form-wrapped phx-change only.
5. Sweep for dead stock content: remove Website/GitHub/Get Started phoenix links everywhere.

VERIFY (the bar): MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors clean; FULL PORT=4002 MIX_ENV=test mix test green (262+, don't break Wallaby journeys — they may assert on page text/selectors; fix test setup ONLY if it asserted stock-Phoenix content); FULL PORT=4002 mix spex green (143). Add a few layout tests (owner sees Schedule link; cleaner does NOT; landing CTAs render). mix format. Final response: files changed, nav structure summary, test counts, "NEEDS RELEASE REBUILD". Under 200 words.
</teammate-message>

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- codemyspec:design: Architecture design, UI design system, and technology strategy. Use before writing code to plan how to build it.
- codemyspec:develop: Full-lifecycle development — context orchestration, LiveView orchestration, and interactive refactoring. Spawns subagents for multi-step workflows.
- codemyspec:implement: Autonomous implementation loop — start or stop requirements-driven development. The agent walks the requirement graph automatically.
- codemyspec:init: Project setup, authentication, and sync. Use when starting a new project, logging in, or refreshing stale state.
- codemyspec:next: Find and start the next requirement task in one gesture. Use after each completed task as your single onboarding instruction.
- codemyspec:product: Product management — guided story interview, review, and Three Amigos sessions. Use when defining what to build, refining requirements, reviewing story quality, or running an Example Mapping session on a story.
- codemyspec:qa: QA testing and issue management — full app QA, per-story QA, integration planning, issue triage, and fixes.
- codemyspec:sync: Sync project components and regenerate architecture views. Use after git pulls, before design sessions, or when views feel stale.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above.
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/rate-card", QuoteLive.RateCard, :edit
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  import Plug.Conn
  import Phoenix.Controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  # Make the remember me cookie valid for 14 days. This should match
  # the session validity setting in UserToken.
  @max_cookie_age_in_days 14
  @remember_me_cookie "_cleaner_crm_web_user_remember_me"
  @remember_me_options [
    sign: true,
    max_age: @max_cookie_age_in_days * 24 * 60 * 60,
    same_site: "Lax"
  ]

  # How old the session token should be before a new one is issued. When a request is made
  # with a session token older than this value, then a new session token will be created
  # and the session and remember-me cookies (if set) will be updated with the new token.
  # Lowering this value will result in more tokens being created by active users. Increasing
  # it will result in less time before a session token expires for a user to get issued a new
  # token. This can be set to a value greater than `@max_cookie_age_in_days` to disable
  # the reissuing of tokens completely.
  @session_reissue_age_in_days 7

  @doc """
  Logs the user in.

  Redirects to the session's `:user_return_to` path
  or falls back to the `signed_in_path/1`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, params \\ %{}) do
    user_return_to = get_session(conn, :user_return_to)

    conn
    |> create_or_extend_session(user, params)
    |> redirect(to: user_return_to || signed_in_path(conn))
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the user out.

  It clears all session data for safety. See renew_session.
  """
  def log_out_user(conn) do
    user_token = get_session(conn, :user_token)
    user_token && Users.delete_user_session_token(user_token)

    if live_socket_id = get_session(conn, :live_socket_id) do
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(live_socket_id, "disconnect", %{})
    end

    conn
    |> renew_session(nil)
    |> delete_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, @remember_me_options)
    |> redirect(to: ~p"/")
  end

  @doc """
  Authenticates the user by looking into the session and remember me token.

  Will reissue the session token if it is older than the configured age.
  """
  def fetch_current_scope_for_user(conn, _opts) do
    with {token, conn} <- ensure_user_token(conn),
         {user, token_inserted_at} <- Users.get_user_by_session_token(token) do
      conn
      |> assign(:current_scope, scope_with_active_account(user))
      |> maybe_reissue_user_session_token(user, token_inserted_at)
    else
      nil -> assign(conn, :current_scope, Scope.for_user(nil))
    end
  end

  defp ensure_user_token(conn) do
    if token = get_session(conn, :user_token) do
      {token, conn}
    else
      conn = fetch_cookies(conn, signed: [@remember_me_cookie])

      if token = conn.cookies[@remember_me_cookie] do
        {token, conn |> put_token_in_session(token) |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)}
      else
        nil
      end
    end
  end

  # Reissue the session token if it is older than the configured reissue age.
  defp maybe_reissue_user_session_token(conn, user, token_inserted_at) do
    token_age = DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(:second), token_inserted_at, :day)

    if token_age >= @session_reissue_age_in_days do
      create_or_extend_session(conn, user, %{})
    else
      conn
    end
  end

  # This function is the one responsible for creating session tokens
  # and storing them safely in the session and cookies. It may be called
  # either when logging in, during sudo mode, or to renew a session which
  # will soon expire.
  #
  # When the session is created, rather than extended, the renew_session
  # function will clear the session to avoid fixation attacks. See the
  # renew_session function to customize this behaviour.
  defp create_or_extend_session(conn, user, params) do
    token = Users.generate_user_session_token(user)
    remember_me = get_session(conn, :user_remember_me)

    conn
    |> renew_session(user)
    |> put_token_in_session(token)
    |> maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(token, params, remember_me)
  end

  # Do not renew session if the user is already logged in
  # to prevent CSRF errors or data being lost in tabs that are still open
  defp renew_session(conn, user) when conn.assigns.current_scope.user.id == user.id do
    conn
  end

  # This function renews the session ID and erases the whole
  # session to avoid fixation attacks. If there is any data
  # in the session you may want to preserve after log in/log out,
  # you must explicitly fetch the session data before clearing
  # and then immediately set it after clearing, for example:
  #
  #     defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
  #       delete_csrf_token()
  #       preferred_locale = get_session(conn, :preferred_locale)
  #
  #       conn
  #       |> configure_session(renew: true)
  #       |> clear_session()
  #       |> put_session(:preferred_locale, preferred_locale)
  #     end
  #
  defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
    delete_csrf_token()

    conn
    |> configure_session(renew: true)
    |> clear_session()
  end

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, %{"remember_me" => "true"}, _),
    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, _params, true),
    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, _token, _params, _), do: conn

  defp write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token) do
    conn
    |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)
    |> put_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, token, @remember_me_options)
  end

  defp put_token_in_session(conn, token) do
    conn
    |> put_session(:user_token, token)
    |> put_session(:live_socket_id, user_session_topic(token))
  end

  @doc """
  Disconnects existing sockets for the given tokens.
  """
  def disconnect_sessions(tokens) do
    Enum.each(tokens, fn %{token: token} ->
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(user_session_topic(token), "disconnect", %{})
    end)
  end

  defp user_session_topic(token), do: "users_sessions:#{Base.url_encode64(token)}"

  @doc """
  Handles mounting and authenticating the current_scope in LiveViews.

  ## `on_mount` arguments

    * `:mount_current_scope` - Assigns current_scope
      to socket assigns based on user_token, or nil if
      there's no user_token or no matching user.

    * `:require_authenticated` - Authenticates the user from the session,
      and assigns the current_scope to socket assigns based
      on user_token.
      Redirects to login page if there's no logged user.

  ## Examples

  Use the `on_mount` lifecycle macro in LiveViews to mount or authenticate
  the `current_scope`:

      defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PageLive do
        use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

        on_mount {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}
        ...
      end

  Or use the `live_session` of your router to invoke the on_mount callback:

      live_session :authenticated, on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
        live "/profile", ProfileLive, :index
      end
  """
  def on_mount(:mount_current_scope, _params, session, socket) do
    {:cont, mount_current_scope(socket, session)}
  end

  def on_mount(:require_authenticated, _params, session, socket) do
    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)

    if socket.assigns.current_scope && socket.assigns.current_scope.user do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must log in to access this page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  def on_mount(:require_sudo_mode, _params, session, socket) do
    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)

    if Users.sudo_mode?(socket.assigns.current_scope.user, -10) do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must re-authenticate to access this page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  defp mount_current_scope(socket, session) do
    Phoenix.Component.assign_new(socket, :current_scope, fn ->
      {user, _} =
        if user_token = session["user_token"] do
          Users.get_user_by_session_token(user_token)
        end || {nil, nil}

      scope_with_active_account(user)
    end)
  end

  # There's no persisted "current account" selection yet (the account
  # picker doesn't write one anywhere), so every account-scoped page
  # would otherwise see a permanently nil `active_account_id`. Until
  # that selection is persisted, default a signed-in user onto one of
  # their accounts — the common case is a single-account owner, for
  # whom this is unambiguous.
  defp scope_with_active_account(nil), do: Scope.for_user(nil)

  defp scope_with_active_account(user) do
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.list_accounts(scope) do
      [account | _] -> %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
      [] -> scope
    end
  end

  @doc "Returns the path to redirect to after log in."
  # the user was already logged in, redirect to settings
  def signed_in_path(%Plug.Conn{assigns: %{current_scope: %Scope{user: %Users.User{}}}}) do
    ~p"/users/settings"
  end

  def signed_in_path(_), do: ~p"/"

  @doc """
  Plug for routes that require the user to be authenticated.
  """
  def require_authenticated_user(conn, _opts) do
    if conn.assigns.current_scope && conn.assigns.current_scope.user do
      conn
    else
      conn
      |> put_flash(:error, "You must log in to access this page.")
      |> maybe_store_return_to()
      |> redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")
      |> halt()
    end
  end

  defp maybe_store_return_to(%{method: "GET"} = conn) do
    put_session(conn, :user_return_to, current_path(conn))
  end

  defp maybe_store_return_to(conn), do: conn
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole do
  @moduledoc """
  Restricts office-only surfaces — scheduling, timesheets (including
  the payroll CSV export), quality, invoices, clients, quotes,
  reminders, and the audit trail — to account owners and admins.

  A cleaner (or anyone with no office role on the active account) is
  redirected to `/field`, their own surface, with an error flash.

  ## Usage

  As a LiveView `on_mount` hook, listed after
  `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth`'s `:require_authenticated` in the same
  `live_session` (it relies on `current_scope.user` already being
  assigned):

      live_session :require_office_role,
        on_mount: [
          {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
          {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
        ] do
        live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
        ...
      end

  As a plug, listed after `:require_authenticated_user` in the
  pipeline, for controller routes such as the timesheet CSV export:

      pipeline :require_office_role do
        plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
      end
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  import Plug.Conn
  import Phoenix.Controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts

  @behaviour Plug

  @impl Plug
  def init(opts), do: opts

  @impl Plug
  def call(conn, _opts) do
    if office_role?(conn.assigns.current_scope) do
      conn
    else
      conn
      |> put_flash(:error, "You don't have access to that page.")
      |> redirect(to: ~p"/field")
      |> halt()
    end
  end

  def on_mount(:default, _params, _session, socket) do
    scope = socket.assigns.current_scope

    if office_role?(scope) do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You don't have access to that page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/field")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  defp office_role?(%{active_account_id: nil}), do: false

  defp office_role?(scope),
    do: Accounts.get_user_role(scope, scope.user.id, scope.active_account_id) in [:owner, :admin]
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth do
  @moduledoc """
  Gates the client portal's LiveViews behind a magic-link session —
  no user login. Reads the client id `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalController`
  wrote to the session's `:portal_client_id` key after a valid
  `/portal/access/:token` exchange, mirroring how
  `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth` reads `:user_token` for staff auth.

  ## Usage

      live_session :portal,
        on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth, :require_client}] do
        live "/portal", PortalLive.Home, :index
      end
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  alias CleanerCrm.Portal

  def on_mount(:require_client, _params, session, socket) do
    case session["portal_client_id"] do
      nil ->
        socket =
          socket
          |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "Please use your portal link to sign in.")
          |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/")

        {:halt, socket}

      client_id ->
        {:cont,
         Phoenix.Component.assign_new(socket, :client, fn -> Portal.get_client!(client_id) end)}
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.Scope do
  @moduledoc """
  Defines the scope of the caller to be used throughout the app.

  The `CleanerCrm.Users.Scope` allows public interfaces to receive
  information about the caller, such as if the call is initiated from an
  end-user, and if so, which user. Additionally, such a scope can carry fields
  such as "super user" or other privileges for use in authorization checks,
  or to ensure specific code paths can only be accessed for a given scope.

  It is useful for logging as well as for scoping pubsub subscriptions and
  broadcasts when a caller subscribes to an interface or performs a particular
  action.

  Feel free to extend the fields on this struct to fit the needs of
  growing application requirements.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  defstruct user: nil,
            active_account: nil,
            active_account_id: nil

  @doc """
  Creates a scope for the given user.

  Returns nil if no user is given.
  """
  def for_user(%User{} = user) do
    %__MODULE__{user: user}
  end

  def for_user(nil), do: nil
end

  @moduledoc """
  Defines the scope of the caller to be used throughout the app.

  The `CleanerCrm.Users.Scope` allows public interfaces to receive
  information about the caller, such as if the call is initiated from an
  end-user, and if so, which user. Additionally, such a scope can carry fields
  such as "super user" or other privileges for use in authorization checks,
  or to ensure specific code paths can only be accessed for a given scope.

  It is useful for logging as well as for scoping pubsub subscriptions and
  broadcasts when a caller subscribes to an interface or performs a particular
  action.

  Feel free to extend the fields on this struct to fit the needs of
  growing application requirements.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  defstruct user: nil,
            active_account: nil,
            active_account_id: nil

  @doc """
  Creates a scope for the given user.

  Returns nil if no user is given.
  """
  def for_user(%User{} = user) do
    %__MODULE__{user: user}
  end

  def for_user(nil), do: nil
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Authorization do
  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  def authorize(action, %Scope{} = scope, resource) do
    case {action, resource} do
      {:read_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        MembersRepository.user_has_account_access?(scope.user.id, account_id)

      {:manage_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        user_role = MembersRepository.get_user_role(scope.user.id, account_id)
        user_role in [:owner, :admin]

      {:manage_members, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        user_role = MembersRepository.get_user_role(scope.user.id, account_id)
        user_role in [:owner, :admin]

      {:delete_account, account_id} when is_binary(account_id) ->
        user_role = MembersRepository.get_user_role(scope.user.id, account_id)
        user_role == :owner

      _ ->
        false
    end
  end

  def authorize!(action, scope, resource) do
    unless authorize(action, scope, resource) do
      raise "Unauthorized: #{action} on #{inspect(resource)}"
    end
  end
end

  @moduledoc """

  Scoped to an account: every client belongs to exactly one account and

  """

  use Ecto.Schema

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,

          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "clients" do
    field :name, :string
    field :active, :boolean, default: true
    field :card_on_file, :boolean, default: false
    field :email, :string
    field :phone, :string
    field :preferred_channel, Ecto.Enum, values: [:email, :sms], default: :email

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    has_many :properties, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

    client

    |> validate_required([:name], message: "is required")
    |> validate_length(:name, min: 1, max: 200)
  end

    |> cast(attrs, [:name, :active, :card_on_file, :email, :phone, :preferred_channel])

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ReminderController do
  @moduledoc """
  Public confirm/reschedule endpoints clients reach from reminder
  messages — reached by the opaque token in the link, no
  authentication.
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications

  def confirm(conn, %{"token" => token}) do
    case Notifications.confirm_reminder(token) do
      {:ok, _notification} -> render(conn, :confirm)
      {:error, :not_found} -> conn |> put_status(:not_found) |> render(:not_found)
    end
  end

  def reschedule(conn, %{"token" => token}) do
    case Notifications.request_reschedule(token) do
      {:ok, _notification} -> render(conn, :reschedule)
      {:error, :not_found} -> conn |> put_status(:not_found) |> render(:not_found)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PortalController do
  @moduledoc """
  The magic-link entry point into the client portal: `GET
  /portal/access/:token` exchanges a token (mailed to the client, or
  handed out at booking) for a portal session — no password
  required.

  ## Dependencies

  - `CleanerCrm.Portal`
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Portal

  def access(conn, %{"token" => token}) do
    case Portal.access_portal(token) do
      {:ok, client_id} ->
        conn
        |> put_session(:portal_client_id, client_id)
        |> redirect(to: ~p"/portal")

      {:error, :invalid} ->
        render(conn, :invalid)
    end
  end
end

2	  @moduledoc """
3	  This module defines the test case to be used by
4	  tests that require setting up a connection.
5	
6	  Such tests rely on `Phoenix.ConnTest` and also
7	  import other functionality to make it easier
8	  to build common data structures and query the data layer.
9	
10	  Finally, if the test case interacts with the database,
11	  we enable the SQL sandbox, so changes done to the database
12	  are reverted at the end of every test. If you are using
13	  PostgreSQL, you can even run database tests asynchronously
14	  by setting `use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true`, although
15	  this option is not recommended for other databases.
16	  """
17	
18	  use ExUnit.CaseTemplate
19	
20	  using do
21	    quote do
22	      # The default endpoint for testing
23	      @endpoint CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint
24	
25	      use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes
26	
27	      # Import conveniences for testing with connections
28	      import Plug.Conn
29	      import Phoenix.ConnTest
30	      import CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase
31	    end
32	  end

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines the test case to be used by
  tests that require setting up a connection.

  Such tests rely on `Phoenix.ConnTest` and also
  import other functionality to make it easier
  to build common data structures and query the data layer.

  Finally, if the test case interacts with the database,
  we enable the SQL sandbox, so changes done to the database
  are reverted at the end of every test. If you are using
  PostgreSQL, you can even run database tests asynchronously
  by setting `use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true`, although
  this option is not recommended for other databases.
  """

  use ExUnit.CaseTemplate

  using do
    quote do
      # The default endpoint for testing
      @endpoint CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

      # Import conveniences for testing with connections
      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.ConnTest
      import CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase
    end
  end

  setup tags do
    CleanerCrmTest.DataCase.setup_sandbox(tags)
    {:ok, conn: Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()}
  end

  @doc """
  Setup helper that registers and logs in users.

      setup :register_and_log_in_user

  It stores an updated connection and a registered user in the
  test context.
  """
  def register_and_log_in_user(%{conn: conn} = context) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = CleanerCrm.Users.Scope.for_user(user)

    opts =
      context
      |> Map.take([:token_authenticated_at])
      |> Enum.into([])

    %{conn: log_in_user(conn, user, opts), user: user, scope: scope}
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the given `user` into the `conn`.

  It returns an updated `conn`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, opts \\ []) do
    token = CleanerCrm.Users.generate_user_session_token(user)

    maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, opts[:token_authenticated_at])

    conn
    |> Phoenix.ConnTest.init_test_session(%{})
    |> Plug.Conn.put_session(:user_token, token)
  end

  defp maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(_token, nil), do: nil

  defp maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at) do
    CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.override_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at)
  end
end

same rationale." 112 def check_field(session, css_selector) do 113 execute_script( 114 session, 115 """ 116 var el = document.querySelector(arguments[0]); 117 el.checked = true; 118 el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true})); 119 el.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true})); 120 """, 121 [css_selector] 122 ) 123 end 124 125 @doc """ 126 A deliberate pause after a click that saves/submits/navigates, or 127 after a fresh `visit`. `assert_has`'s own retry (default 3s) doesn't 128 reliably cover either gap in this environment — confirmed by 129 repeated runs across every journey, not a guess: without it, clicks 130 and field fills intermittently land on a not-yet-settled DOM (a 131 save's redirect not yet landed, or a sibling autofocus hook still 132 racing for the field being filled). 133 """ 134 def settle(session, ms \\ 1000) do 135 Process.sleep(ms) 136 session 137 end 138 end 139

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.QualityLive.TemplatesTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers issue 35ce3856: `CleanerCrm.Quality.ChecklistTemplate` had no
  UI to create one and no wiring to a job's checklist, so proof-of-work
  was unreachable through the live product without seeded data. No
  spex/BDD story owns this surface, so it's covered here instead.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.ClientsFixtures
  alias CleanerCrm.Quality
  alias CleanerCrm.SchedulingFixtures
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  setup %{conn: conn} do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)
    {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})
    scope = %{scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}

    client = ClientsFixtures.client_fixture(scope, %{name: "Riverside Bungalow"})
    property = ClientsFixtures.property_fixture(scope, client, %{service_address: "1 Main St"})

    conn = log_in_user(conn, user)

    %{conn: conn, scope: scope, client: client, property: property}
  end

  test "create_checklist_template supports sort/drop params and a blank property_id",
       %{scope: scope, property: property} do
    {:ok, template} =
      Quality.create_checklist_template(scope, %{
        "name" => "Standard Clean",
        "property_id" => "",
        "items" => %{
          "0" => %{"room" => "Kitchen", "task" => "Wipe counters", "required" => "true"},
          "1" => %{"room" => "Bathroom", "task" => "Sanitize", "required" => "false"}
        }
      })

    assert template.property_id == nil
    assert length(template.items) == 2

    {:ok, updated} =
      Quality.update_checklist_template(scope, template, %{
        "property_id" => property.id,
        "items" => %{
          "0" => %{"room" => "Kitchen", "task" => "Wipe counters", "required" => "true"},
          "1" => %{"room" => "Bathroom", "task" => "Sanitize", "required" => "false"}
        },
        "items_drop" => ["1"]
      })

    assert updated.property_id == property.id
    assert length(updated.items) == 1
    assert hd(updated.items).task == "Wipe counters"
  end

  test "an empty-items create_checklist picks up the job's property template",
       %{scope: scope, client: client, property: property} do
    {:ok, _template} =
      Quality.create_checklist_template(scope, %{
        "name" => "Standard Clean",
        "property_id" => property.id,
        "items" => %{
          "0" => %{"room" => "Kitchen", "task" => "Wipe counters", "required" => "true"},

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Accept do @moduledoc """ Token-link quote acceptance (story 849): the locked price recap, slot selection, cancellation-policy agreement, and card capture that converts a `CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead` into a client + property + plan/job and issues portal access. Mounted as the `:accept` `live_action` of `CleanerCrmWeb.BookingLive.Quote` rather than routed on its own — see that module's moduledoc for why (`push_patch/2` only navigates within the currently-mounted view module, and the calculator patches here once contact info locks in a price). Every function below still only ever touches `CleanerCrm.Booking`. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Booking` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :html alias CleanerCrm.Booking alias CleanerCrm.Booking.Lead alias CleanerCrm.Money @doc "Loads the lead for `token` and sets up whichever step it's currently at." def mount(token, socket) do case Booking.get_lead_by_token(token) do nil -> socket |> assign(:page_title, "Booking not found") |> assign(:step, :not_found) |> assign(:lead, nil) %Lead{} = lead -> socket |> assign(:page_title, "Confirm your booking") |> assign(:lead, lead) |> assign(:slot_form, to_form(Booking.change_slot(lead), as: :booking)) |> assign(:confirmation_form, to_form(Booking.change_confirmation(lead), as: :booking)) |> assign(:slot_unavailable, false) |> assign(:policy_required, false) |> assign(:step, step_for(lead)) end end defp step_for(%Lead{status: :converted}), do: :confirmed defp step_for(%Lead{status: :payment_pending}), do: :payment_pending defp step_for(%Lead{status: :payment_declined}), do: :payment_declined defp step_for(%Lead{scheduled_date: nil}), do: :select_slot defp step_for(%Lead{}), do: :confirm def render(assigns) do ~H""" <.header>Confirm your booking

We couldn't find that booking link. It may have expired — please request a new quote.

Your price

{Money.format_cents(@lead.total_cents)}

Locked in from your instant quote — no added fees.

You're booked for {format_date(@lead.scheduled_date)} at {format_time(@lead.start_time)}. Check your email for a link to your client portal.
Confirming your payment — this page will update as soon as it's done.
Your card was declined. Please try a different card below.
That time was just booked by someone else — please pick another slot.
<.form :if={@step == :select_slot} for={@slot_form} id="slot-form" data-test="slot-form" phx-submit="select_slot" > <.input field={@slot_form[:scheduled_date]} type="date" label="Date" /> <.input field={@slot_form[:start_time]} type="time" label="Start time" />
<.button phx-disable-with="Checking...">Continue
<.form :if={@step in [:confirm, :payment_declined]} for={@confirmation_form} id="confirmation-form" data-test="confirmation-form" phx-submit="confirm_booking" >

Cancellation policy: cancel or reschedule at least 24-hour ahead of your visit to avoid a late-cancellation fee.

<.input field={@confirmation_form[:policy_agreed]} type="checkbox" label="I agree to the cancellation policy" data-test="policy-agreement-checkbox" />

Please agree to the cancellation policy to continue.

<%!-- Real card capture (Stripe Elements) is deferred — this mirrors the existing `/pay/:token` payment page's own simplification, a single test card baked in as a hidden field until Elements lands. --%>
<.button phx-disable-with="Booking..."> Confirm & pay {Money.format_cents(@lead.total_cents)}
""" end def handle_event("select_slot", %{"booking" => params}, socket) do case Booking.select_slot(socket.assigns.lead, params) do {:ok, slotted_lead} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:lead, slotted_lead) |> assign(:step, :confirm)} {:error, changeset} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :slot_form, to_form(changeset, as: :booking))} end end def handle_event("confirm_booking", %{"booking" => params}, socket) do case Booking.confirm_booking(socket.assigns.lead, params) do {:ok, updated} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:lead, updated) |> assign(:step, :payment_pending) |> assign(:policy_required, false) |> assign(:slot_unavailable, false)} {:error, :policy_required} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:policy_required, true) |> assign(:slot_unavailable, false)} {:error, :slot_unavailable} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:slot_unavailable, true) |> assign(:policy_required, false)} # Defense in depth (issue 4e985412): the slot-selection form # itself now rejects a past date/time, but a slot picked as # "later today" can still go stale by the time the client # reaches this step — send them back to pick a new one rather # than leave them stuck retrying a confirmation that can never # succeed. {:error, :slot_in_past} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:step, :select_slot) |> assign(:slot_form, to_form(Booking.change_slot(socket.assigns.lead), as: :booking)) |> assign(:policy_required, false) |> assign(:slot_unavailable, false) |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash( :error, "That time has already passed — please pick another slot." )} {:error, _reason} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:slot_unavailable, true) |> assign(:policy_required, false)} end end defp format_date(date), do: Calendar.strftime(date, "%B %-d, %Y") defp format_time(time), do: Calendar.strftime(time, "%-I:%M %p") end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.ReviewLive.Public do @moduledoc """ The public, token-link review page a client reaches from their review-request email: a 1-5 star rating plus optional text, one-tap submission. A rating of 4-5 publishes the review; 3 or below routes it to a private complaint sent to the owner instead. Route: `/reviews/:token`. No login — reached from a mailed link, so it lives in the `:current_user` style `live_session` (mounts `current_scope` for the root layout without requiring one). ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Reviews` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Reviews alias CleanerCrm.Reviews.Review @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H"""
This review link is invalid.
<.header>How was your cleaning?
<.button type="submit" data-test="submit-review-button" class="mt-2"> Submit Review
Thank you! Your review is on its way to being published.
Thanks for letting us know — we've sent your note directly to the owner.
""" end @impl true def mount(%{"token" => token}, _session, socket) do case Reviews.get_review_by_token(token) do nil -> {:ok, assign(socket, review: nil, rating: nil, submitted: false)} %Review{status: :review_requested} = review -> {:ok, assign(socket, review: review, rating: nil, submitted: false)} %Review{} = review -> {:ok, assign(socket, review: review, rating: review.rating, submitted: true)} end end @impl true def handle_event("set_rating", %{"rating" => rating}, socket) do {:noreply, assign(socket, :rating, String.to_integer(rating))} end def handle_event("submit_review", %{"review" => params}, socket) do do_submit(socket, socket.assigns.submitted, socket.assigns.rating, params) end defp do_submit(socket, true, _rating, _params), do: {:noreply, socket} defp do_submit(socket, false, nil, _params) do {:noreply, put_flash(socket, :error, "Please select a rating first.")} end defp do_submit(socket, false, rating, params) do case Reviews.submit_review(socket.assigns.review, rating, Map.get(params, "text")) do {:ok, updated} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, review: updated, submitted: true)} {:error, _changeset} -> {:noreply, put_flash(socket, :error, "Something went wrong.")} end end end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb do
  @moduledoc """
  The entrypoint for defining your web interface, such
  as controllers, components, channels, and so on.

  This can be used in your application as:

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :controller
      use CleanerCrmWeb, :html

  The definitions below will be executed for every controller,
  component, etc, so keep them short and clean, focused
  on imports, uses and aliases.

  Do NOT define functions inside the quoted expressions
  below. Instead, define additional modules and import
  those modules here.
  """

  use Boundary, deps: [CleanerCrm], exports: :all

  def static_paths, do: ~w(assets fonts images favicon.ico robots.txt)

  def router do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Router, helpers: false

      # Import common connection and controller functions to use in pipelines
      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.Controller
      import Phoenix.LiveView.Router
    end
  end

  def channel do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Channel
    end
  end

  def controller do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Controller, formats: [:html, :json]

      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      import Plug.Conn

      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def live_view do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveView

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def live_component do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.LiveComponent

      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  def html do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.Component

      # Import convenience functions from controllers
      import Phoenix.Controller,
        only: [get_csrf_token: 0, view_module: 1, view_template: 1]

      # Include general helpers for rendering HTML
      unquote(html_helpers())
    end
  end

  defp html_helpers do
    quote do
      # Translation
      use Gettext, backend: CleanerCrmWeb.Gettext

      # HTML escaping functionality
      import Phoenix.HTML
      # Core UI components
      import CleanerCrmWeb.CoreComponents

      # Common modules used in templates
      alias Phoenix.LiveView.JS
      alias CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts

      # Routes generation with the ~p sigil
      unquote(verified_routes())
    end
  end

  def verified_routes do
    quote do
      use Phoenix.VerifiedRoutes,
        endpoint: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint,
        router: CleanerCrmWeb.Router,
        statics: CleanerCrmWeb.static_paths()
    end
  end

  @doc """
  When used, dispatch to the appropriate controller/live_view/etc.
  """
  defmacro __using__(which) when is_atom(which) do
    apply(__MODULE__, which, [])
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.UserSessionControllerTest do
  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures
  alias CleanerCrm.Users

  setup do
    %{unconfirmed_user: unconfirmed_user_fixture(), user: user_fixture()}
  end

  describe "POST /users/log-in - email and password" do
    test "logs the user in", %{conn: conn, user: user} do
      user = set_password(user)

      conn =
        post(conn, ~p"/users/log-in", %{
          "user" => %{"email" => user.email, "password" => valid_user_password()}
        })

      assert get_session(conn, :user_token)
      assert redirected_to(conn) == ~p"/"

      # Now do a logged in request and assert on the menu
      conn = get(conn, ~p"/")
      response = html_response(conn, 200)
      assert response =~ user.email
      assert response =~ ~p"/users/settings"
      assert response =~ ~p"/users/log-out"
    end

    test "logs the user in with remember me", %{conn: conn, user: user} do
      user = set_password(user)

      conn =
        post(conn, ~p"/users/log-in", %{
          "user" => %{
            "email" => user.email,
            "password" => valid_user_password(),
            "remember_me" => "true"
          }
        })

      assert conn.resp_cookies["_cleaner_crm_web_user_remember_me"]
      assert redirected_to(conn) == ~p"/"
    end

    test "logs the user in with return to", %{conn: conn, user: user} do
      user = set_password(user)

      conn =
        conn
        |> init_test_session(user_return_to: "/foo/bar")
        |> post(~p"/users/log-in", %{
          "user" => %{
            "email" => user.email,
            "password" => valid_user_password()
          }
        })

      assert redirected_to(conn) == "/foo/bar"
      assert Phoenix.Flash.get(conn.assigns.flash, :info) =~ "Welcome back!"
    end

    test "redirects to login page with invalid credentials", %{conn: conn, user: user} do
      conn =
        post(conn, ~p"/users/log-in?mode=password", %{
          "user" => %{"email" => user.email, "password" => "invalid_password"}
        })

      assert Phoenix.Flash.get(conn.assigns.flash, :error) == "Invalid email or password"
      assert redirected_to(conn) == ~p"/users/log-in"
    end
  end

  describe "POST /users/log-in - magic link" do
    test "logs the user in", %{conn: conn, user: user} do
      {token, _hashed_token} = generate_user_magic_link_token(user)

      conn =
        post(conn, ~p"/users/log-in", %{
          "user" => %{"token" => token}
        })

      assert get_session(conn, :user_token)
      assert redirected_to(conn) == ~p"/"

      # Now do a logged in request and assert on the menu
      conn = get(conn, ~p"/")
      response = html_response(conn, 200)
      assert response =~ user.email
      assert response =~ ~p"/users/settings"
      assert response =~ ~p"/users/log-out"
    end

    test "confirms unconfirmed user", %{conn: conn, unconfirmed_user: user} do
      {token, _hashed_token} = generate_user_magic_link_token(user)
      refute user.confirmed_at

      conn =
        post(conn, ~p"/users/log-in", %{
          "user" => %{"token" => token},
          "_action" => "confirmed"
        })

      assert get_session(conn, :user_token)
      assert redirected_to(conn) == ~p"/"
      assert Phoenix.Flash.get(conn.assigns.flash, :info) =~ "User confirmed successfully."

      assert Users.get_user!(user.id).confirmed_at

      # Now do a logged in request and assert on the menu
      conn = get(conn, ~p"/")
      response = html_response(conn, 200)
      assert response =~ user.email
      assert response =~ ~p"/users/settings"
      assert response =~ ~p"/users/log-out"
    end

    test "redirects to login page when magic link is invalid", %{conn: conn} do
      conn =
        post(conn, ~p"/users/log-in", %{
          "user" => %{"token" => "invalid"}
        })

      assert Phoenix.Flash.get(conn.assigns.flash, :error) ==
               "The link is invalid or it has expired."

      assert redirected_to(conn) == ~p"/users/log-in"
    end
  end

@doc """
  Logs the given user into the Wallaby `session` via the real password
  form. Each actor in a multi-actor journey test should get their own
  session (via `@sessions N` / `%{sessions: [...]}`) rather than
  logging out and back in on one session — Wallaby has no cookie-clear
  helper, and juggling one session between actors doesn't match how
  two real people would use the app at once anyway.

  Two timing quirks, both confirmed by repeated runs, not guesses:

  - The magic-link form's email input carries `phx-mounted={JS.focus()}`
    (autofocus on connect). If the password form's email field is
    filled before that hook fires, the steal-focus race sometimes
    empties it back out mid-keystroke — so this waits a beat after
    `visit` before touching either field.
  - The password form submits over the LiveView socket first, which
    just flips `phx-trigger-action` to make the JS client re-submit it
    a second time as a real native POST (the only way to actually
    write the session cookie) — so this waits for something that only
    exists after that second, real submission lands, not just for the
    click's own socket round-trip.
  """
  def log_in(session, user, password) do
    import Wallaby.Query

    session = visit(session, "/users/log-in")
    Process.sleep(500)

    session
    |> fill_in(css("#login_form_password_email"), with: user.email)
    |> fill_in(css("#user_password"), with: password)
    |> click(button("Log in only this time"))
    |> assert_has(link("Log out"))
  end

defp load_jobs(socket) do
    scope = socket.assigns.current_scope
    date = socket.assigns.date

    jobs =
      scope
      |> Scheduling.list_jobs_for_week(week_start(date))
      |> Enum.filter(&(&1.scheduled_date == date and &1.cleaner_id == scope.user.id))
      |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.start_time, Time)

    assign(socket, :jobs, jobs)
  end

  # `CleanerCrm.Notifications` (story 843) may not exist yet, or may
  # land after this view does — read defensively so this view never
  # needs to change again for that context to wire in. Expected
  # contract: `list_unacknowledged/1` returns every account-wide
  # pending schedule-change alert; filtered here to this cleaner's own.
  defp load_notifications(socket) do
    scope = socket.assigns.current_scope
    cleaner_id = scope.user.id

    notifications =
      if Code.ensure_loaded?(CleanerCrm.Notifications) and
           function_exported?(CleanerCrm.Notifications, :list_unacknowledged, 1) do
        scope
        |> CleanerCrm.Notifications.list_unacknowledged()
        |> Enum.filter(&(&1.cleaner_id == cleaner_id))
      else
        []
      end

    assign(socket, :notifications, notifications)
  end

  defp week_start(date), do: Date.add(date, -(Date.day_of_week(date) - 1))

  defp parse_date(nil), do: nil

  defp parse_date(string) do
    case Date.from_iso8601(string) do
      {:ok, date} -> date

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.LayoutsTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers the role-aware app nav built for the UI/navigation pass: an
  office role (owner/admin) gets the full grouped nav, everyone else
  signed in gets just "My Day" — and the two must never both render.
  `/field` is reachable by both roles, so it's the one route these
  tests can share.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts

  describe "nav_role/1 and signed_in_home/1" do
    test "signed out has no role and no signed-in home" do
      assert Layouts.nav_role(nil) == nil
      assert Layouts.signed_in_home(nil) == nil
    end
  end

  describe "role-aware nav on /field" do
    setup %{conn: conn} do
      owner = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
      owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)
      {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(owner_scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})

      member = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
      {:ok, _member} = Accounts.add_user_to_account(owner_scope, member.id, account.id, :member)

      %{conn: conn, owner: owner, member: member}
    end

    test "an owner sees the office nav, not the cleaner's My Day link",
         %{conn: conn, owner: owner} do
      {:ok, _view, html} = conn |> log_in_user(owner) |> live(~p"/field")

      assert html =~ ~s(data-test="office-nav")
      assert html =~ ~p"/schedule"
      assert html =~ "Field view"
      refute html =~ ~s(data-test="cleaner-nav")
    end

    test "a cleaner sees only My Day, no office nav", %{conn: conn, member: member} do
      {:ok, _view, html} = conn |> log_in_user(member) |> live(~p"/field")

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.LayoutsTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers the role-aware app nav built for the UI/navigation pass: an
  office role (owner/admin) gets the full grouped nav, everyone else
  signed in gets just "My Day" — and the two must never both render.
  `/field` is reachable by both roles, so it's the one route these
  tests can share.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts

  describe "nav_role/1 and signed_in_home/1" do
    test "signed out has no role and no signed-in home" do
      assert Layouts.nav_role(nil) == nil
      assert Layouts.signed_in_home(nil) == nil
    end
  end

  describe "role-aware nav on /field" do
    setup %{conn: conn} do
      owner = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
      owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)
      {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(owner_scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})

      member = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
      {:ok, _member} = Accounts.add_user_to_account(owner_scope, member.id, account.id, :member)

      %{conn: conn, owner: owner, member: member}
    end

    test "an owner sees the office nav, not the cleaner's My Day link",
         %{conn: conn, owner: owner} do
      {:ok, _view, html} = conn |> log_in_user(owner) |> live(~p"/field")

      assert html =~ ~s(data-test="office-nav")
      assert html =~ ~p"/schedule"
      assert html =~ "Field view"
      refute html =~ ~s(data-test="cleaner-nav")
    end

    test "a cleaner sees only My Day, no office nav", %{conn: conn, member: member} do
      {:ok, _view, html} = conn |> log_in_user(member) |> live(~p"/field")

      assert html =~ ~s(data-test="cleaner-nav")
      refute html =~ ~s(data-test="office-nav")
      refute html =~ ~p"/schedule"
    end
  end

content.text:
I've completed the app shell and navigation build and reported back to the team lead. Summary of what was done:

**Core change**: `lib/cleaner_crm_web/components/layouts.ex` now has a role-aware `Layouts.app` with a `variant` attribute (`:app` for authenticated surfaces, `:portal` for the client portal, `:public` for landing/booking/token pages), computing the office/cleaner role once per render via `CleanerCrm.Accounts.get_user_role`, defensively guarded against nil accounts and wrapped in try/rescue.

**Navigation built**:
- Office (owner/admin): direct links to Schedule/Clients/Quotes/Invoices/Timesheets/Quality/Reviews, grouped "More" (Reminders/Audit) and "Settings" (Rate card/Booking policy/Accounts/Integrations/User settings) dropdowns, a Field view link, and a user dropdown — collapsing into one hamburger below the `lg` breakpoint.
- Cleaner/member: just "My Day", always visible (not hidden behind a hamburger, since mobile is their primary device) plus the same user dropdown, no office links.
- Portal: Home/Invoices nav. Public/token pages (landing, `/book`, payment, reminder, review, portal-invalid pages): minimal logo + "Client portal" link only.

**Landing page** (`page_html/home.html.heex`) replaced entirely with a real Cleaner CRM hero and CTAs, including a conditional "Go to app" link for signed-in visitors.

**Cleanup**: removed the duplicate top-strip menu from `root.html.heex` and every stock phoenixframework.org/GitHub/"Get Started" reference across the app.

**Verification**: compiles clean with warnings-as-errors, `mix format` clean, full test suite (266 tests, 0 failures) and spex suite (143 tests, 0 failures) both green on port 4002, including all Wallaby journey tests. Two pre-existing tests and one shared test helper needed updates because they asserted on the old stock/duplicate header behavior rather than product requirements — those are detailed in the message to the team lead. The running release on port 4100 and dev build were left untouched throughout.
